topics.label: Lecture framing and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's scope and learning objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Mutational and epigenetic drivers of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cellular changes drive tumor development, extending the mutation-based account of clonal selection to question whether mutations alone explain transformation.

topics.label: Stemness and the cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy influences its capacity to initiate or propagate cancer.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness and cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that permit previously mutated cells to develop into tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive surrounding cells and the therapeutic opportunities created by that dependence.

topics.label: Methods for studying cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular and spatial analysis of tissue specimens can reveal tumor evolution and interactions within the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Converging conditions for malignant evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic develops an integrated account of why malignant outgrowth requires favorable conditions to coincide, extending that account to developmental timing and childhood cancer.

topics.label: Lecture close and preview of cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces therapy as the subject of the next session.
